newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran petrochemical capacity expected to climb. [CORRECTED 06:52 GMT 02/12]
newsitem.headline: Iran petrochemical capacity expected to climb. [CORRECTED 06:52 GMT 02/12]

text.p: Iran's annual petrochemical production capacity is expected to reach 16 million tonnes by 1999 (corrects from 2000), an Iranian official said on Sunday.

The official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted Mansour Moazami, director of National Petrochemical Industries, as saying annual production capacity stands at 13.5 million tonnes. (Corrects to add dropped word "capacity")
He said the industry's output reached nine million tonnes last year and predicted that Iran would produce 10 million tonnes in 1996.
Iran has set ambitious plans to boost revenue from petrochemicals and natural gas over the next ten years despite U.S. efforts to choke its oil industry.

Under the original second five-year plan from 1995-2000, Iran is scheduled to build five complexes worth $3.3 billion that would increase total petrochemical capacity to an annual 15 million tonnes from 10 million at present.
The Islamic republic is the second largest producer of petrochemicals in the Middle East, behind Saudi Arabia.

Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh has said Tehran would boost annual income from petrochemical exports to $6 billion from a current $408 million by more than tripling output to 35 million tonnes in 10 years.
He said Iran expected to earn annually $2 billion to $3 billion from gas exports by the year 2000.
